subject: Cognitive Science
title: The Invisible Gorilla
description: A quick win: understand The Invisible Gorilla.

hook.text: In a famous experiment, half the viewers missed a person in a gorilla suit walking through a game.

buildup.text: They were counting basketball passes. Focused on the task, they literally didn't see the gorilla.

discovery.text: This is inattentional blindness—when you focus hard on one thing, you become blind to others.

twist.text: It's not about eyesight. The gorilla hit their retinas. Their brain just never processed it.

climax.text: Simons and Chabris showed that attention isn't just a filter—it shapes what you consciously see.

punchline.text: You can look right at something and never see it.

quiz.question: What is inattentional blindness?
options: Failing to see things when focused elsewhere

details.summary: In a famous experiment by Simons and Chabris, people counting basketball passes failed to notice a person in a gorilla suit walking through the scene. This inattentional blindness demonstrates that we can be completely blind to unexpected events when our attention is elsewhere.
details.whyItMatters: Inattentional blindness proves that seeing requires attention, not just open eyes. It explains why drivers miss pedestrians and why eyewitness testimony can be unreliable.
takeaways: Focused attention can cause blindness to obvious events
About half of participants missed the gorilla entirely
Inattentional blindness affects everyone regardless of expertise

faq.question: Does knowing about inattentional blindness prevent it?
faq.answer: Knowing about the phenomenon helps only slightly. People who expect something unusual may catch it, but they become blind to other unexpected events instead. The fundamental limitation of attention persists regardless of awareness.

faq.question: How does inattentional blindness affect real life?
faq.answer: It contributes to traffic accidents where drivers look but fail to see motorcycles or pedestrians. Radiologists can miss tumors on scans when focused on other findings. It affects any situation where attention is directed narrowly at one task.
